sentences.text: This claim petition emanates in respect of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner by name Harisha in respect of the Road Traffic Accident dated 08.02.2023.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:

That on 08.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding his Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ES- SCCH 15 3 MVC No.2347/2023 2977 very slowly and cautiously, observing all traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near Hebbal ring road, near Angali stone shop, Hebbal, at that time, respondent's Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-0894 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle, resulting in the accident.
It is submitted that the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries all over the body due to the impact of the accident.
3. Immediately, after the accident petitioner was shifted to Baptist hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with cost and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
4. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.2 remained absent and he was placed exparte.

SCCH 15 4 MVC No.2347/2023 Respondent No.1 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.1 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending car bearing Reg.No.KA-01- AH-0894 in favour of the respondent No.2.
The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the car did not have valid and effective driving license.
The age, avocation of the petitioner is denied.
The petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. Vide order dated 19.12.2023 the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-

sentences.text: ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 08.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m., on Hebbal SCCH 15 5 MVC No.2347/2023 ring road, Angali Stone Shop, Hebbal, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-0894?

2) Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for? If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3) What Order or Award?
6.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 18 and the Respondent No.1 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 & 2 and relied upon Ex.R1 and 2.

The Learned Counsel for the petitioner has relied on the following citation:
(2018) 7 Supreme Court Cases 558, between Amrit Paul Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., & others.

sentences.text: Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for parties in this case.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 8. Issue No.1: Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the petitioner that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-0894.
9.

In this regard the petitioner got himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination he has deposed that on 08.02.2023 at about 4.30 p.m. when he was riding his scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ES-2977 all of a sudden driver of the SCCH 15 7 MVC No.2347/2023 offending vehicle came from the opposite direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the scooter resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.

sentences.text: The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of the accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR which discloses that the case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC on the basis of Ex.P2 - Complaint given on 21.02.2023.

As far as the delay in lodging the complaint is concerned the petitioner has deposed that the car driver assured to bear the expenses and later he did not pay the amount and hence there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
The said reason assigned in the complaint appears to be satisfactory for delay in giving the complaint.
Ex . P3 - spot mahazar discloses that the accident has taken place in the middle of the road at about 40 feet wide and it is double road.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet which discloses that SCCH 15 8 MVC No.2347/2023 the case has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC and Sec.134(b) and 187 of IMV Act.

It is mentioned in the charge sheet that the driver of the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner from Hebbala towards Nagavara service road and dashed the scooter from the front side resulting in the injuries to the petitioner.
Hence these documents discloses that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

11. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for respondent No.1, PW.1 has deposed that he was taking treatment at Baptist hospital and hence there is a delay in giving the complaint.
He has deposed that his father and the car driver took him to the hospital and he has intimated the doctor about the accident in the hospital.
Except the suggesting that a false complaint is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to SCCH 15 9 MVC No.2347/2023
prove negligence on the part of the petitioner.

Except the suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the negligence on the petitioner side nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence or rashness on the part of petitioner.
The petitioner has clearly and categorically deposed about the manner of the accident.
The oral testimony of PW.1 has stood unrebutted and PW1 has withstood the cross- examination of Respondent No.1.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
PW.1 has also declined the suggestion imputing the cause of the accident to be due to his negligence.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
SCCH 15 10 MVC No.2347/2023 In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 in the above accident.

In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.
12. Issue No.2:
In view of the findings on issue No.1 in favour of petitioner, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The computation of compensation will have to be decided separately under various heads.

sentences.text: MEDICAL OR TREATMENT EXPENSES:

The petitioner has produced Ex.P7 which is discharge summary of Bengaluru Baptist hospital which shows that the petitioner was admitted on 08.02.2023 and discharged on 11.02.2023 and he had sustained fracture of both bones of right forearm and abrasion 3X1 cm over right fore arm.
The petitioner has produced Ex.P10 - medical bills.

As far as medical bills are concerned SCCH 15 11 MVC No.2347/2023 PW.1 is cross-examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and in the cross-examination except suggesting that the bills are created nothing is elicited to disprove the authenticity of the said bills.
Hence petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.1,09,418/- under this head.
13. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

As per the medical documents the petitioner has fracture of both bones of right forearm and abrasion over right forearm and it is stated in the petition that injuries sustained and physical impairment has caused unbearable pain and weakness in the right hand,
unable to fold the right wrist and lift weights or do any work as prior to the accident.
It is not possible to ascertain quantum of compensation admissible to petitioner for the mental trauma, pain and sufferings etc., which he actually suffered due to the accidental injuries.

Keeping in view the trauma and nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.30,000/- is SCCH 15 12 MVC No.2347/2023 awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
14. LOSS OF ACTUAL EARNINGS:
In his evidence PW.1 has submitted he was aged about 39 years and he was Administrative Manager at Eureka Co. Ltd., and drawing Rs.85,000/- p.m.
The medical records reflect that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries which has resulted in the disability and hence certainly he is unable to resume his work as prior to the accident.
It is submitted by the petitioner was drawing Rs.85,000/- per month.
However in his cross- examination he has deposed that he has not produced any documents to prove his income.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the Petitioner it would be proper to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the notional income as on the date of the accident, as per the guidelines of Lok-Adalat chart.

As per the relevant period the notional income is taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.
Taking into consideration that the petitioner due to the injuries might not SCCH 15 13 MVC No.2347/2023 have been in a position to work for at least 6 months hence
, as such the petitioner is entitled to an amount of Rs.16,000 X 6 = 96,000/- under this head.
15. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS DUE TO DISABILITY:

The petitioner has claimed in his affidavit that he had sustained permanent disability to his hand and in order to prove the same he got examined Orthopedic surgeon as PW.2 and PW.2 in his evidence deposed that the petitioner has sustained physical impairment and it is not progressive and not likely to improve in future and submitted that he assessed disability of the right arm as 39% and whole body disability is 13%.
PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner is unable to fold the wrist unable to type and lift weights, wasting of the right forearm muscles, restricted right wrist movements.
PW.2 is cross
- examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and PW.2 in the cross-examination has denied that he has falsely assessed the disability in order to help the petitioner.

PW.2 has deposed that he has assessed the Harsha.H vs Bajaj All Gen Ins Co Ltd on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161932331/
5 SCCH 15 14 MVC No.2347/2023 disability as per the guidelines.

sentences.text: Nothing much is elicited in the cross-examination of PW.2 to disprove the disability assessed by PW.2.

Accordingly, above mentioned disability can be read read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in Bajaj Allianz Insurance Company Limited Vs Union of India.

sentences.text: The evidence of PW.2 discloses that the petitioner had sustained 13% disability to the whole body.
The monthly income of the petitioner is already assessed at Rs.16,000/- at the relevant time.
As far as, age of the petitioner at the time of the accident is concerned on perusal of the petitioner's Aadhaar card Ex.P11 the date of birth of the petitioner is 05.05.1984.
Going by the same, the age of petitioner as on date of accident i.e., 08.02.2023 was around 39 years.

Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2347/2023 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

sentences.text: SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '15' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of his above disability.

The loss of future earnings of petitioner due to his above injury and permanent physical disability comes to Rs.3,74,400/- (Rs.16,000/- X 12 X 15 X 13%) and the same is awarded to him as compensation under this head.
16. Loss of Amenities:

In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the extent of permanent physical disability and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
17. Attendant's charges, Special diet and Conveyance:
The facts show that physical condition of the petitioner is such that he might have to taken the help of an attendant.
Further, he would be requiring conveyance for movement.
His avocation has been hit due to his disablement.
He might have spent considerable amount towards special diet during his SCCH 15 16 MVC No.2347/2023 treatment.
Therefore, petitioner is granted Rs.20,000/- under this head.
18. COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
It is stated in the evidence of PW.2 that Petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of the implant and the estimate of this surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced estimation.
However, by considering the further surgery, it is proper to grant compensation of 20,000/-.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

19. TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :

Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.
RAJASTAN VS. SMT. LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 6,69,818/- with costs SCCH 15 18 MVC No.2347/2023 and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

21. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AH-0894.
However the liability of the insurance company is subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

In this regard respondent insurance company has contended that there is a breach of the policy conditions and in this regard got examined the official of RTO as RW.1 and in his evidence has deposed that the offending vehicle is a motor cab number KA-01-AH-0894 and had permit only from 06.07.2017 to 05.07.2022 and there was no permit on 08.02.2023 which is the date of the accident.
Further he deposed that as per the Ex.R2 the permit is canceled from 13.02.2023 and as per the Ex.R3 the permit is obtained from 22.02.2023 to 21.02.2028.
Hence it is submitted that as on the date of the accident there was no permit to the offending SCCH 15 19 MVC No.2347/2023 vehicle.
RW.1 has denied that only when permit is existing it can be canceled on 13.02.2023.

RW.1 deposed that before 08.02.2023 the vehicle has been transferred and Harish i.e.,

22.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the same the respondent insurance company has got examined its Assistant Manager as RW.2 who has deposed that the owner of the offending vehicle has availed permit on 22.03.2023 and the vehicle was used in public place without having a permit which is a violation of the contract of insurance and hence stated that the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
The petitioner has taken contention that absence of permit is not mentioned in the charge sheet and the cab had national permit.
However, it was the duty of respondent No.1 to produce the copy of the permit in order to establish that the offending vehicle had permit as on the date of the accident.

On the other hand on perusal of Ex.R2 it discloses that the permit obtained by one Darshan Devaiah S/o Medappa is from SCCH 15 20 MVC No.2347/2023 06.07.2017 to 05.07.2022 and Ex.R3 also discloses that the permit is obtained at Bengaluru Central RTO which is valid from 22.02.2023 to 21.02.2028.
Hence the owner of the offending vehicle has remained absent and has failed to produce the permit pertaining to the cut off period.
Hence there is no documentary evidence to show that the offending vehicle had permit as on the date of the accident.

23. In this regard the learned counsel for petitioner has also relied on the decision in (2018) 7 SCC 558, between Amrit paul Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., & other and it is submitted that since the vehicle was 3000 kg there is no necessity of obtaining permit.

entities.text: Amrit paul Singh and another Vs. TATA AIG Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., & other
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However the said provision is applicable to goods vehicle and not for transport vehicle.
The offending vehicle in this case was used as a transport vehicle as a cab without any valid permit and it is not a case of deviation of permit, but absence of permit.
Hence the said case law is not applicable facts of the case.

Since there was no permit as on the date of the accident, there SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2347/2023 is a breach of policy condition and hence the insurance company is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2 and it is respondent No.2 who will have to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is "Partly in the Affirmative".
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.2 U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner against respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.
The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of 6,69,818/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to SCCH 15 22 MVC No.2347/2023 deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that PW.1 suffered grievous injuries on account of rashness and negligence of driver driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Therefore, in view of the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Corporation and another (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given SCCH 15 15 MVC No.2347/2023 in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
Regarding rate of interest: As far as the rate of interest is concerned the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS.
RAJASTAN VS. SMT. LAXMI reported in 2018 (4) AKR 808 has held that in case of motor accident claims rate of interest awarded is 6% per annum and the Hon'ble High court has been consistently granting 6% interest in Motor Vehicles Accident Claims and Compensation cases.
However, it was the duty of respondent No.1 to produce the copy of the permit in order to establish that the offending vehicle had permit as on the date of the accident.
Hence the owner of the offending vehicle has remained absent and has failed to produce the permit pertaining to the cut off period.
Hence there is no documentary evidence to show that the offending vehicle had permit as on the date of the accident.
The offending vehicle in this case was used as a transport vehicle as a cab without any valid permit and it is not a case of deviation of permit, but absence of permit.
Hence the said case law is not applicable facts of the case.
Since there was no permit as on the date of the accident, there SCCH 15 21 MVC No.2347/2023 is a breach of policy condition and hence the insurance company is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2 and it is respondent No.2 who will have to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

The remaining 25% award amount shall be deposited as F.D. in the name of the Petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of three years.
The Advocate fee is fixed at 1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
